source: Quiz 4 - Sessions 1-5: Building and Improving Agent Skills
question: How can identical prompts produce different responses when the trained weights stay fixed?

options.text: Each response trains a different set of weights before starting.
options.feedback: Ordinary generation uses trained weights. Different samples can produce different text without an additional training step.

options.text: Sampling can choose different tokens and change later context.
options.feedback: A different early token creates a different continuation context. Later token choices can then follow another path.

options.text: Each prompt causes the model to create a different vocabulary.
options.feedback: A new vocabulary is not required for variation. Selection among the existing vocabulary can lead to different responses.

options.text: Attention randomly selects a complete response from a database.
options.feedback: Attention combines contextual information. It does not retrieve one complete answer from a response database.
